Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testToClass_object()` calls `ClassUtils.toClass()` with an Object array containing `String`, `null`, and `Double` elements, expecting the output to be a Class array with corresponding `String.class`, `null`, and `Double.class`. The bug report states that `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` throws a NullPointerException (NPE) on a null element in the array.

Examining the implementation of the method `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` reveals the root cause: The code loops over each element of the input array and directly calls `.getClass()` on each element without null-checking:
```java
for (int i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    classes[i] = array[i].getClass();
}
```
Calling `.getClass()` on a `null` element causes a NullPointerException, exactly as described. The test deliberately includes `null` in the array to verify correct behavior. However, the method does not handle this case gracefully.

The correct behavior would be to include `null` in the result array for `null` input elements rather than throwing an exception.

The recent bug reports retrieved do not seem related to this issue, as they focus on different classes and scenarios.

In summary, the bug occurs because the `ClassUtils.toClass` method does not check for `null` elements before invoking `.getClass()`, leading to NPEs on arrays containing nulls. The test expects `null` to appear in the output array in those positions, but the current implementation fails to do so.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
